title: Menu at a café
paragraphs: There is a small, cosy café called "Stepnoy Corner" — or "Corner of the Steppe" in Kazakh — located just five minutes on foot from the WKU main gate. It opened six months ago and has quickly become one of the most popular spots among WKU students. The café is decorated in warm earth tones with dried wildflowers in small vases on every table, photographs of the Kazakh steppe on the walls, and soft traditional music playing in the background.

The menu at Stepnoy Corner is a clever mix of traditional Kazakh dishes and international favourites, with a strong emphasis on fresh, locally sourced ingredients. The owner, a cheerful woman named Gulnaz, grew up in a small village near Uralsk and learned to cook from her grandmother. "I want every customer to feel like they are eating at my grandmother's table," she says with a warm smile.

For breakfast, the café serves freshly baked baursak — soft, fluffy fried dough balls that are a staple of Kazakh cuisine — alongside thick cream and a small pot of wild berry jam. There is also scrambled eggs with fresh herbs, millet porridge with butter and honey, and a selection of hot drinks: traditional black tea served in a piala (a small ceramic bowl), aromatic green tea with mint, and rich, creamy shubat — fermented camel milk, which is considered a health drink in Kazakhstan.

The lunch menu is where Stepnoy Corner really shines. The star dish is beshbarmak — wide flat noodles served with tender boiled lamb, a fragrant broth, and thinly sliced onions. This is the national dish of Kazakhstan and is traditionally served at celebrations and family gatherings. Gulnaz's version uses meat from a local farm and follows her grandmother's original recipe. A portion costs 2,200 tenge and is large enough to share between two people. There is also sorpa — a clear, deeply flavourful lamb broth — served with a side of fresh bread for 850 tenge.

For lighter appetites or vegetarian customers, the café offers manty — large steamed dumplings filled with minced meat and onion — or a vegetarian version filled with pumpkin and potato. There is also a popular salad called Stepnoy — a mix of roasted beetroot, walnuts, dried cranberries, goat's cheese, and rocket leaves dressed with a honey-mustard vinaigrette. It is both beautiful and delicious, and has become a favourite among students who want something healthy but satisfying.

The drinks menu deserves special attention. Besides the traditional teas, the café serves freshly squeezed juices — watermelon, carrot and ginger, and apple and cinnamon are the most popular flavours. In summer, Gulnaz makes a house-made ayran — a cold, slightly salty yoghurt drink — which is absolutely refreshing after a long lecture. All drinks are made fresh to order, and there are no artificial flavourings or preservatives in anything on the menu.

Prices at Stepnoy Corner are very reasonable for students. Most main dishes cost between 1,500 and 2,500 tenge. The daily set lunch — which changes every day and includes a starter, a main course, and a drink — is just 1,800 tenge. This makes it one of the most affordable places to eat near the university while still enjoying high-quality, home-cooked food. The café accepts both cash and bank cards, and has a student discount card: after ten visits, your eleventh drink is free.

Kamila and her friends visit Stepnoy Corner at least twice a week. "I love this place because the food tastes like home," says Kamila. "Every time I eat Gulnaz's beshbarmak, I think of my mother's kitchen in Aktobe." For any WKU student who misses home cooking, feels tired of cafeteria food, or simply wants a peaceful place to study with a good cup of tea — Stepnoy Corner is absolutely the right address. 🍵

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Zhibek, have you tried the new café near the main gate? It's called Stepnoy Corner.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: No, not yet! What's it like? I heard it serves traditional food.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: It's wonderful! The owner cooks everything herself — beshbarmak, manty, baursak... all homemade.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: That sounds amazing. How much is the beshbarmak?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: 2,200 tenge — but it's huge! Enough for two people, easily. I usually share it with Amir.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: What about vegetarian options? I don't eat meat.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: They have pumpkin manty and a really good salad with beetroot and goat's cheese. You'll love them!

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: And to drink? I'm not a big tea drinker.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Freshly squeezed juices! Watermelon, apple-cinnamon, carrot-ginger... all made fresh to order.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: OK, I'm convinced. How about lunch there tomorrow after our English class?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Perfect! They have a daily set lunch for 1,800 tenge — starter, main, and a drink. Great value!

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Brilliant. I'll bring Rustam too — he's always hungry after football training!

grammarNote:
Одно из самых важных различий в английском — исчисляемые и неисчисляемые существительные. Это правило влияет на артикль, форму глагола и выбор quantifier (сколько?).

🔢 ИСЧИСЛЯЕМЫЕ (Countable) — можно посчитать поштучно:
① Имеют единственное И множественное число: apple / apples, student / students
② Можно использовать: a/an, one, two, three, many, a few, each, every
③ Примеры: a book, two chairs, three friends, many students, each lesson
"There is A chair." · "There are THREE chairs." · "I have A question."

💧 НЕИСЧИСЛЯЕМЫЕ (Uncountable) — нельзя посчитать поштучно:
① Только единственное число — множественного НЕТ
② Нельзя: "one water", "two waters", "a rice"
③ Используй: some, any, much, a little, a lot of
④ Частые неисчисляемые: water, milk, tea, rice, bread, money, time, information, advice, news, music, homework, luggage
"I need SOME water." · "There is A LITTLE time." · "She gave me SOME advice."

💡 Универсальные quantifiers (работают с обоими типами):
some / any / a lot of / lots of / plenty of / no
"I have some water." (uncountable) ✅
"I have some apples." (countable) ✅

⚠️ Самые частые ошибки:
❌ "an information" → ✅ "some information" / "a piece of information"
❌ "many homeworks" → ✅ "a lot of homework" (uncountable!)
❌ "advices" → ✅ "advice" (всегда без -s!)
❌ "a news" → ✅ "the news" / "a piece of news"
